job.title: Territory Product Specialist - Commercial Equipment Sales - Premium Global Brand
job.description:
Build Your Career in Commercial Sales - Not Just Demonstrations 
This is a commercial field sales role, not an operational or “on-the-tools” position. 

You will work with a globally recognised premium brand, engaging commercial end users to demonstrate, educate and influence the adoption of high-performance equipment solutions. 
Operating across Perth and regional WA, you will partner with councils, contractors, facilities teams and commercial organisations, delivering structured product demonstrations while building pipeline and supporting revenue growth. 
This role is best suited to someone who already brings foundational sales experience and is looking to further develop their career in a hands-on, customer-facing commercial environment, and offers a clear pathway into Account Management or Business Development. 
Our client is renowned for engineering excellence, product reliability and an extensive national dealer network; the organisation continues to invest heavily in product innovation, customer support and long-term market growth.
  
What This Role Involves: 
This is a hybrid of field sales and technical demonstration, where success is driven by your ability to:
  • Engage customers in a professional, consultative sales approach 
  • Deliver structured demonstrations that educate, influence and convert 
  • Build relationships with commercial end users and stakeholders 
  • Identify opportunities and develop a sustainable territory pipeline 
  • Work alongside dealers to support conversion from demonstration to sale 
You are not just demonstrating equipment - you are shaping buying decisions and driving commercial outcomes. 
  
What’s In It For You: 
  • $100,000 + Super + Vehicle + Bonus 
  • Structured onboarding and product training 
  • Strong mentorship from experienced commercial leaders
  • Autonomy to manage your own territory 
  • Exposure to a premium global brand and dealer network 
  • Clear long-term career pathways into Account Management or BDM 
Importantly, this role offers both career progression and the opportunity to build a stable, long-term position (3+ years) within a high-performing commercial team.
 
Key Responsibilities: 
  • Develop and manage a defined WA territory 
  • Identify and engage commercial end users across multiple sectors 
  • Deliver professional, structured product demonstrations 
  • Build and maintain a pipeline of opportunities 
  • Influence customer decision-making through education and insight 
  • Partner with dealers to convert opportunities into sales 
  • Maintain strong follow-up, reporting and territory discipline 
  • Travel across metro and regional WA as required 
What You Will Bring: 
  • Minimum 2+ years’ sales experience (essential) 
  • Confidence engaging commercial customers and stakeholders 
  • Ability to deliver clear, structured product demonstrations 
  • Strong communication and influencing capability 
  • Commercial mindset with a focus on outcomes and conversion 
  • Self-driven approach to territory development and pipeline building 
  • Strong organisation and time management skills 
  • Current driver’s licence 
Industry experience is not limited to outdoor power equipment - our client would also welcome candidates from broader technical, equipment or commercial product environments. 
  
Ideal Backgrounds: 
We are prioritising candidates with commercial and demonstration-led experience, including: 
  • Technical or equipment sales roles 
  • Product demonstration or specialist sales positions 
  • Trade, industrial or capital equipment environments 
  • Roles adjacent to Business Development or Account Management 
(Industry sectors such as construction, facilities, industrial or similar are relevant- landscaping backgrounds are not required.) 
  
About the Opportunity:
This is a career-building commercial role within a globally respected organisation known for product innovation, engineering excellence and a strong dealer network. 

You will work closely with an experienced Business Development leader while developing your own presence in market - combining hands-on demonstration capability with structured sales development. 
  
This role will suit someone who: 
  • Already has a foundation in sales 
  • Enjoys being in the field with customers 
  • Wants to build a long-term commercial career 
  • Values both stability and progression 
If you’re ready to step into a true commercial field sales role with strong demonstration capability, we’d love to speak with you.

We’re recruiting for a large, highly regarded and growing insurance organisation looking for customer-focused people to join its Home Claims team in Kawana Waters.
And you don’t need insurance or claims experience to apply.

You bring the people skills. They’ll provide the training, systems knowledge and support to build your career in insurance.

  • $74,140.61 package (inclusive of super) + incentives
  • Permanent, full-time position offering stability and career development
  • Comprehensive paid training – no previous insurance experience required
  • Saturday shift only once every 7–8 weeks
  • Convenient Kawana Waters location close to shops, cafés and restaurants

You’ll manage your own portfolio of home claims, keeping customers informed from start to finish while working with builders, engineers, suppliers and internal teams to move each claim forward.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication
  • Empathy and the ability to build rapport quickly
  • Confidence dealing with different personalities and situations
  • The ability to stay calm during difficult or emotional conversations
  • Good judgement and problem-solving skills
  • Strong attention to detail
  • The ability to organise your workload and manage competing priorities
  • Confidence using technology and learning new systems
  • Accountability, integrity and professionalism
  • A positive attitude and willingness to learn
Hours & roster This is a permanent full-time role working 37.5 hours per week on a rotating roster.
Current operating hours are 6:00am–6:00pm, Monday to Saturday, with a Saturday shift currently required only once every 7–8 weeks.
Your next career move could start here You don’t need to already work in insurance to build a successful career in it.
If you’re looking for stability, comprehensive training, great employee benefits and genuine opportunities to develop and progress, this is an excellent chance to take the customer service experience you already have and turn it into something more.

job.title: Team Leader - Housing Support
job.description:
This is an opportunity to step into a meaningful leadership role with a highly regarded, values-driven not-for-profit organisation supporting veterans and their families across Queensland and the Northern Territory
The role leads a team delivering housing and homelessness support to people who may be experiencing financial hardship, housing instability, homelessness or complex personal circumstances. The service is holistic, practical and deeply person-centred, with a strong focus on dignity, respect and long-term outcomes.

This position will suit an experienced Team Leader, Senior Practitioner or Senior Case Manager who enjoys leading people, improving practice and creating the structure needed for high-quality service delivery.

Why this role?

• $110,000 + super + salary packaging benefits
• Brisbane based
• Leadership-focused role with a small, manageable caseload
• Lead a passionate housing support team across multiple locations (QLD & NT)
• Opportunity to influence practice standards, process improvement and service delivery
• Join a nationally respected, purpose-driven Not for Profit organisation
• Strong systems, structure and operational support
• Support meaningful outcomes for veterans and their families
• Collaborative, values-led and supportive team culture
• Opportunity to contribute to service improvement, process development and best-practice case management
• Exposure across metro, regional and multidisciplinary service environments
• Travel opportunities across regional locations as required
• Stable organisation with strong leadership and long-term community impact

As Team Leader – Housing Support, you will provide day-to-day leadership to a team of Housing Support Practitioners delivering support to veterans and families who are at risk of, or experiencing, homelessness.
The program provides case management, housing support, financial hardship support and, in some cases, funded crisis accommodation. The role has a strong operational focus, including case oversight, referral allocation, quality assurance, staff supervision, stakeholder engagement, financial approvals and compliance with service delivery requirements.
This is primarily a leadership and operational oversight role, with a small caseload held as part of a broader multidisciplinary team.
The role reports to the Wellbeing Manager, Veteran Services and is accountable for leading Housing Support Practitioners within the broader wellbeing team. The position includes leadership across multiple locations, regular case reviews, monitoring caseloads, ensuring compliance, stakeholder collaboration and oversight of case plans and expenditure.

Key responsibilities
In this role, you will:
• Lead, coach and support Housing Support Practitioners across multiple locations
• Provide supervision, case reviews and guidance on complex matters
• Review referrals and allocate work across the team
• Monitor caseloads, workload, risks and team capacity
• Support client-centred, strengths-based housing support and case management
• Review and approve case plans, financial assistance and support requests
• Ensure accurate documentation, case notes and compliance within client systems
• Build strong relationships with internal teams, community organisations, government bodies and specialist housing providers
• Support team culture, performance, engagement and professional development
• Contribute to service improvement, process development and consistent practice standards

About you
You will bring a strong combination of people leadership, case management experience and operational discipline.
You may come from housing, homelessness, community services, mental health, family support, domestic and family violence, AOD, veteran services or another complex case management environment.
You do not need to have worked in veteran services before. What matters is your ability to lead a team, work within structured service delivery requirements, manage competing priorities and support people through complex and sensitive circumstances.

You will bring:
• A degree in Human Services, Health Sciences, Social Work, Psychology, Counselling or a related discipline
• Eligibility for registration or professional membership with a relevant body such as AASW, AHPRA or PACFA
• 2–3+ years’ experience in a Team Leader, Senior Practitioner, Senior Case Manager or similar leadership role (ideally lead a remote multi-state team)
• Strong experience in person-centred and strengths-based case management
• Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor and motivate staff
• Strong attention to detail, documentation and compliance
• Sound judgement when working with complex or sensitive client situations
• Ability to work within policies, procedures, legislative requirements and budget parameters
• Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills
• A Queensland C Class driver’s licence
• Flexibility to travel when required

Experience in specialist homelessness services or community services will be highly regarded. An understanding of the ADF, Defence or veteran community would also be beneficial, but is not essential.

The environment
You will be joining a supportive and collaborative team that is genuinely committed to the people they support.
This is a role with heart, but it also requires structure. The successful candidate will be comfortable working in a process-driven environment where case notes, compliance, financial approvals, service standards and clear communication all matter.
The best fit will be someone who can bring empathy and professionalism, while also creating consistency, accountability and confidence across the team.

job.title: Quarry Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Quarry Maintenance Supervisor - Afternoon Shift

Lead the Future of Maintenance at One of Queensland's Premier Quarry Operations

Petrie, Brisbane QLD | Permanent Full-Time
Build something from the ground up.
This isn't just another maintenance supervisor role.
We're looking for an experienced leader to establish and lead a newly created afternoon maintenance function at one of Queensland's busiest quarry operations. This is an opportunity to make a genuine impact by improving equipment reliability, reducing downtime and creating a high-performing maintenance culture.
If you thrive on leading people, solving complex mechanical challenges and driving continuous improvement, we'd love to hear from you.

The Opportunity
Reporting into the Quarry Leadership Team, you'll lead a dedicated afternoon maintenance crew responsible for maintaining both fixed and mobile plant across the site.
This role has been created to maximise planned maintenance outside of peak production hours, giving your team greater access to equipment and enabling proactive maintenance that keeps the operation running at its best.
You'll be trusted to lead your team, improve maintenance processes and influence operational performance.

What You'll Be Doing
  • Lead and mentor a team of maintenance tradespeople.
  • Coordinate preventative, planned and reactive maintenance activities.
  • Improve plant reliability and equipment availability.
  • Plan and supervise shutdown maintenance.
  • Coordinate contractors and specialist service providers.
  • Promote a proactive safety culture and ensure compliance with site standards.
  • Work closely with operations to minimise downtime and maximise production.
  • Identify and implement continuous improvement initiatives.

About You
You'll be a hands-on leader who enjoys developing people and improving plant performance. Ideally, you'll bring:
  • Trade qualification in Mechanical Fitting, Diesel Fitting or a related discipline.
  • Previous experience leading maintenance teams.
  • Strong fixed plant maintenance experience within quarrying, mining, cement, heavy manufacturing or industrial processing.
  • Experience maintaining crushing, screening and conveying equipment.
  • Strong knowledge of hydraulics, gearboxes, pumps and rotating equipment.

job.description:
We are pleased to partner with our waste management company in Yennora NSW for an Accounts Receivable Officer to join their team.  Ideally, you will be familiar with liquid waste as this will facilitate a smoother transition to the role and allow easier adaptation, particularly as they are rolling out a new operating and finance system.

Key responsibilities: 
  • Process high volumes of invoices
  • Generate and issue credit notes
  • Ensure customers are billed correctly and respond to queries promptly via email and phone.
  • Identify and resolve invoicing and data processing issues
  • Interpret operational processes, job management systems, and contracts to facilitate accurate invoicing
  • Manage month-end processes, including sales accruals and customer spend analysis
  • Collate disposal/destruction of documents
  • Maintain updated customer records and terms
  • Support with the update of commission sheets

  • Debtors Management - daily debtor contact and attendance/leading weekly debtor meetings

  • Hazardous and dangerous waste

  • Environmental services
